title: Launching a New Homestay Online: A 90-Day Checklist
excerpt: A week-by-week 90-day plan for launching a new homestay online, from state registration and photos to Google, OTA listings and first reviews.
description: A 90-day checklist to launch a new homestay online: registration, photos, Google Business Profile, OTA listings, soft launch and first reviews.
html:
Launching a new homestay online takes about 90 days of steady work: register with the right authorities, photograph the property, set up Google Business Profile and WhatsApp Business, list on one or two OTAs, host your first guests, and collect your first reviews. Do it in that order, because each step depends on the one before.

Before day one: registration and paperwork

Many Indian states run their own homestay or bed-and-breakfast registration schemes through the state tourism department, and the rules, documents and benefits differ from state to state. Do not rely on a neighbour's experience or an old forum post. Check your state tourism department's website or office directly for the current scheme, and ask your local panchayat or municipality about any trade licence or local permissions.

Also check, with your accountant, whether you need GST registration, how you will issue invoices, and how you will keep guest records and ID copies as required by local police. Open a business bank account in the property's name before you take any payments. Sorting this out first saves you from relisting or correcting documents later.

The 90-day launch plan at a glance

WeeksFocusKey tasksDone when
1–2FoundationsRegistration application, business bank account, property name, phone number, email, policies writtenYou can legally take a booking and receive payment
3Photos and copyPrepare rooms, shoot photos in daylight, write room descriptions, house rules and how-to-reach directionsA folder of approved photos and a shared document of text
4Google and WhatsAppSignboard up, Google Business Profile created and verification started, WhatsApp Business with catalogue and quick repliesProfile submitted, WhatsApp ready to answer enquiries
5First OTAList on one platform that suits your guests, set cancellation policy and seasonal pricesListing live and bookable
6Calendar and second OTAMaster calendar, iCal sync where available, optional second platformNo date can be booked twice
7–8Soft launchHost friends, family and their contacts at a fair rate in exchange for honest feedback; fix what they findTeething problems sorted
9–10First paying guestsAnswer enquiries fast, follow a check-in and check-out routine, ask every guest for a reviewFirst few genuine reviews on Google and the OTA
11Website and socialSimple website with rooms, location and contact; Instagram with host story and regular postsGuests can find you outside the OTA
12–13Review and adjustCheck enquiries by source, conversion to bookings, review themes, pricing; plan next quarterA written plan for months four to six

Weeks 1 to 4: foundations, photos and Google

Name and contact details

Choose a name you will keep, check that nobody nearby uses something similar, and secure a matching Instagram handle and website domain if you can. Pick one phone number for guests and use it on every listing. Write the name, address and phone in a master document and copy it exactly everywhere.

Photos

Finish the rooms before you photograph them. Shoot on a bright day, with beds made, curtains open, bathrooms spotless and clutter removed. Cover each room type, each bathroom, common areas, food, the view and the approach road. These photos will be used on every platform for months, so take the time.

Google Business Profile and WhatsApp Business

Put up a signboard, then create or claim your Google Business Profile with the correct lodging category and an accurate map pin. Verification can take time, so start it early. Set up WhatsApp Business with a catalogue of rooms and quick replies for rates, how to reach, advance policy and confirmation.

Weeks 5 and 6: listings and calendar

Start with one OTA rather than five. Choose the one your likely guests use: Airbnb for travellers who value the host and setting, MakeMyTrip or Goibibo for many domestic leisure travellers, Booking.com or Agoda if you expect international guests. Learn the extranet, set your policies and pricing calendar, and only add a second platform when you are confident your calendar stays accurate.

Before you go live, create a master calendar that every family member updates. Use iCal sync between platforms where it is available, and check daily. Our post on homestay listing optimisation on Airbnb, Booking.com and MakeMyTrip covers photo order, descriptions and pricing in more detail.

Weeks 7 to 10: soft launch and first reviews

Your first stays will reveal problems you never noticed: a geyser that takes too long, a confusing turn on the road, a room that is noisy in the morning. A soft launch with people you know lets you fix these before strangers write reviews.

  • Write a simple check-in routine: welcome, Wi-Fi password, meal timings, house rules, emergency contact.
  • Write a check-out routine: settle the bill, thank the guest, ask for a review.
  • Ask soft-launch guests for honest written feedback, and fix the top three issues before paying guests arrive.
  • For genuine paying guests, send a review link the day after checkout. Never offer discounts in exchange for reviews or post reviews yourself.
  • Reply to every review, positive or negative, within a few days.

Early reviews carry a lot of weight for a new listing, so the quality of your first few stays matters more than how many bookings you get.

Weeks 11 to 13: website, social media and review

A simple website

Once operations are steady, build a simple website: home page, one page per room type, a "how to reach" page, a "things to do nearby" page and a contact page with WhatsApp and map. It does not need an online booking engine yet. It gives Google more to show and gives guests a direct way to reach you.

Instagram

Set up Instagram with your host story in the bio and post a few times a week about the place, the food, the neighbourhood and the hosts. Keep the rhythm modest so it lasts.

The day-90 review

At the end of the quarter, sit down with your booking sheet and answer:

  • How many enquiries came from each source, and how many became bookings?
  • What did reviews praise, and what did they complain about?
  • Which dates went unsold, and was price or visibility the reason?
  • What would you do differently in the next 90 days?

What to leave for later

New owners often spend money early on things that can wait: a custom booking engine, paid ads before there are reviews, many OTA listings at once, branded merchandise, or an agency retainer before the basics exist. Get the foundations, listings and first reviews right first. Paid advertising works better once guests clicking an ad can see good photos and real reviews.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need to register my homestay before listing it online?

Requirements differ by state and by platform. Many states have their own homestay registration scheme run by the state tourism department, and some OTAs ask for registration or licence details during listing. Check your state tourism department's current rules and any local permissions before you start, and keep copies of all documents ready for platform verification and guest queries.

Which OTA should a new homestay list on first?

Pick one platform that matches your likely guests and run it well before adding more. Airbnb suits properties with a strong host story and unusual setting; MakeMyTrip and Goibibo reach many domestic leisure travellers; Booking.com and Agoda bring more international guests. Adding several at once increases the risk of double bookings while you are still learning.

How do I get my first reviews?

Make the first stays excellent, then ask. Speak to each guest at checkout, then send a review link by WhatsApp the next day with a short thank-you. Reply to every review. Never offer discounts or gifts for reviews, never post reviews yourself, and do not ask family to post them. Platforms detect and remove fake reviews, and it can harm your listing.

When should a new homestay start paid advertising?

Usually after the first two or three months, once your listings have good photos, clear details and a few genuine reviews. Ads send people to your profile or listing, and without reviews many will not book. Start with a small test budget, track enquiries and confirmed bookings rather than clicks, and expand only what works.

Where to start

This week, check your state tourism department's homestay registration scheme and open a business bank account. Then block a day to prepare and photograph the rooms, and put up your signboard so you can start Google verification. Print the 90-day table above and tick off each week. For low-cost ideas once you are live, read our guide to marketing a small resort or homestay on a tight budget, or see the hospitality page.
